data.title: Flaky Test
data.tagline: A flaky test sometimes passes and sometimes fails when the code has not changed.
data.learningOutcome: You can recognize flakiness from alternating red and green on one version and first inspect waiting, shared resources, and environment differences.
data.description: The same CI commit can time out occasionally, or parallel tests can race for one account and alternate red and green. Unlike a defect that fails every time, flakiness makes the result untrustworthy. Retries can collect clues or temporarily reduce impact, but do not replace finding timing, shared-state, or environment causes.

learning.assumes: You know automated tests should give stable results under the same conditions.
learning.outcome: You can recognize flakiness from alternating red and green on one version and first inspect waiting, shared resources, and environment differences.

distinctions.label: Regression test
distinctions.explanation: A Flaky Test alternates between pass and fail even when code is unchanged. A Regression Test should reliably judge whether a change broke existing behavior.

explanation.title: Confirm unchanged code, changing result
explanation.text: Passing and failing on the same version and case points to an uncontrolled test, environment, or concurrency condition. A case that always fails is more like a reproducible defect and needs a different path.

explanation.title: Look for observable sources of variance
explanation.text: Check whether the test waits for a true completion signal, cases share an account or port, data remains, or CI differs from local. Record failure frequency and logs, then fix the cause.

data.boundary: A flaky test is neither an ordinary one-off failure nor a test fixed by retries. Retries can temporarily continue a pipeline or gather reproduction information, but unaddressed flakiness makes teams stop trusting red lights.

lessonPractice.title: A login test on the same commit passes, passes, fails, passes, then fails, and both failures time out. What should you do first?

options.label: Keep run evidence, inspect wait conditions, shared accounts, and CI differences, then make it reproduce stably
options.feedback: Correct. Alternating results on unchanged code are evidence of variance, so find the uncontrolled factor.

options.label: Set retries to infinite until the pipeline turns green
options.feedback: That hides signal and adds time; it does not remove the instability cause.

options.label: Treat it directly like a defect that always reproduces, without comparing run conditions
options.feedback: It may reveal a real product issue too, but first distinguish why the same test sometimes passes.

data.agentPrompt: This login test times out intermittently on the same commit. Run it repeatedly and retain each log, inspect wait conditions, shared accounts, and test data; find a reproducible source of variance before merely increasing retries.
